blocks.text: Dohra:

Half of the Khalsa contingent which had started earlier, Soon did it cross to the other side of the river Beas. Listen to the way the Khalsa occupied Doab region, After slaughtering the caretaker of Dina Beg's1 territory. (1)
lines: Half of the Khalsa contingent which had started earlier,
Soon did it cross to the other side of the river Beas.
Listen to the way the Khalsa occupied Doab region,
After slaughtering the caretaker of Dina Beg's1 territory.

blocks.text: Chaupai:

Bishambar Dass2 was the name of their Kshtriya caretaker, Of village Lisara was he a resident earlier. In the service of Dina Beg's wife (after her husband's death), Was Bishambar Dass the chief among the caretakers. (2)
lines: Bishambar Dass2 was the name of their Kshtriya caretaker,
Of village Lisara was he a resident earlier.
In the service of Dina Beg's wife (after her husband's death),
Was Bishambar Dass the chief among the caretakers.

blocks.text: Twenty five thousand troops did he keep under his command, Many a canon and medium guns did he possess. Many a hill chief did he have as his allies, For waging a war had he invited them indeed. (3)
lines: Twenty five thousand troops did he keep under his command,
Many a canon and medium guns did he possess.
Many a hill chief did he have as his allies,
For waging a war had he invited them indeed.

blocks.text: Half the Khalsa Dal (Taruna Dal) advised Bisambar dass, That he must go in hot pursuit of the Buddha Dal3 . As the Buddha Dal could not fight without their younger compatriots, He could easily chase Buddha Dal out of Doab. (4)
lines: Half the Khalsa Dal (Taruna Dal) advised Bisambar dass,
That he must go in hot pursuit of the Buddha Dal3 .
As the Buddha Dal could not fight without their younger compatriots,
He could easily chase Buddha Dal out of Doab.

blocks.text: Thus did Bishambar Dass go after them from Dina Nagar4 , Doaba region did he enter after crossing the Beas. Putting up a camp a few miles behind their camp, He sent a written challenge to the Buddha Dal Singhs. (5)
lines: Thus did Bishambar Dass go after them from Dina Nagar4 ,
Doaba region did he enter after crossing the Beas.
Putting up a camp a few miles behind their camp,
He sent a written challenge to the Buddha Dal Singhs.

blocks.text: Dohra:
Thus did he write a message to the Singhs: If they were desirous of their survival and well-being. Must they vacate the Doaba region forth with, Surely would he eliminate them if they tarried. (6)
lines: Thus did he write a message to the Singhs: If they were desirous of their survival and well-being.
Must they vacate the Doaba region forth with,
Surely would he eliminate them if they tarried.

blocks.text: Chaupai:

Highly incensed did the Singhs feel hearing this, A resolution did they pass holding a congregation. Must they occupy his territory after killing the Kshtriya upstart, As it was an excellent opportunity for the Khalsa's cause. (7)
lines: Highly incensed did the Singhs feel hearing this,
A resolution did they pass holding a congregation.
Must they occupy his territory after killing the Kshtriya upstart,
As it was an excellent opportunity for the Khalsa's cause.

blocks.text: A ransom money from him should they demand first, Which he would not pay and would speak foul. Thus did the Khalsa send a message to him, Must he pay the ransom if he wished to live. (8)
lines: A ransom money from him should they demand first,
Which he would not pay and would speak foul.
Thus did the Khalsa send a message to him,
Must he pay the ransom if he wished to live.

blocks.text: From his side did he send his response, Ransom would he pay only if the entire Khalsa Panth demanded. Must the Buddha Dal vacate his Doaba territory, Thereafter would he send a ransom after them. (9)
lines: From his side did he send his response,
Ransom would he pay only if the entire Khalsa Panth demanded.
Must the Buddha Dal vacate his Doaba territory,
Thereafter would he send a ransom after them.

blocks.text: Dohra:
Then did the Khalsa write him back again: The person who refused to pay ransom now, How could they trust him to pay later on, After they had vacated his territory at his bidding? (10)
lines: Then did the Khalsa write him back again: The person who refused to pay ransom now,
How could they trust him to pay later on,
After they had vacated his territory at his bidding?

blocks.text: Chaupai:

The Singhs asked Bishambhar Dass to ger ready for a fight, Lest he should blame them for not informing him in advance, (Late) Dina Beg had an agreement with the Singhs, That never would he ever fight with the Singhs. (11)
lines: The Singhs asked Bishambhar Dass to ger ready for a fight,
Lest he should blame them for not informing him in advance,
(Late) Dina Beg had an agreement with the Singhs,
That never would he ever fight with the Singhs.

blocks.text: That is why had the Singhs informed him in advance, It was upto him either to be their ally or to fight with them. Bishambhar Dass asked them to have it out with him, It was better they looked after themselves than to threaten him. (12)
lines: That is why had the Singhs informed him in advance,
It was upto him either to be their ally or to fight with them.
Bishambhar Dass asked them to have it out with him,
It was better they looked after themselves than to threaten him.

blocks.text: He threatened them to be ready for an attack, It would be better they vacated the Doaba territory. Thus did both enter into verbal slangs against each other, As both were adamant not to budge from their positions. (13)
lines: He threatened them to be ready for an attack,
It would be better they vacated the Doaba territory.
Thus did both enter into verbal slangs against each other,
As both were adamant not to budge from their positions.

blocks.text: It was a moment for the Kshtriya to suffer ignominy, It was a moment for the Khalsa to gain in strength. Putting up his army's camp near Urmar Tanda5 , Bisambhar Dass wished to face the Singhs in direct encounter. (14)
lines: It was a moment for the Kshtriya to suffer ignominy,
It was a moment for the Khalsa to gain in strength.
Putting up his army's camp near Urmar Tanda5 ,
Bisambhar Dass wished to face the Singhs in direct encounter.

blocks.text: Dohra:

After Dina Beg (the Jalandhar custodian) had expired, Bishambhar Dass had doubled his army in strength. Vainglorious had he become after this increased number, As well as at the support of the forces of the hill chiefs. (15)
lines: After Dina Beg (the Jalandhar custodian) had expired,
Bishambhar Dass had doubled his army in strength.
Vainglorious had he become after this increased number,
As well as at the support of the forces of the hill chiefs.

blocks.text: Chaupai:

Gathering intelligence about the Singhs' movements, He found the Singhs scattered on looting errands. Hoping to take over the Singhs' camp in their absence, He launched an attack with such aspirations. (16)
lines: Gathering intelligence about the Singhs' movements,
He found the Singhs scattered on looting errands.
Hoping to take over the Singhs' camp in their absence,
He launched an attack with such aspirations.

blocks.text: Like a swarm of locusts did he dispatch his troops, Which soon did reach the Buddha Dal Singhs' camp. The Singhs, on their side, were already prepared for a fight, Though small in number were they there in their base camp. (17)
lines: Like a swarm of locusts did he dispatch his troops,
Which soon did reach the Buddha Dal Singhs' camp.
The Singhs, on their side, were already prepared for a fight,
Though small in number were they there in their base camp.

blocks.text: For once his troops did push the Singhs back, As their horses crushed the Singhs under their hooves. But as the Singh chiefs stood to bear the enemy brunt, Thousands of Singhs arrived after hearing the exchange of fire. (18)
lines: For once his troops did push the Singhs back,
As their horses crushed the Singhs under their hooves.
But as the Singh chiefs stood to bear the enemy brunt,
Thousands of Singhs arrived after hearing the exchange of fire.

blocks.text: The way an insectivorous bird pounces upon white ants, So did the Singhs pounce upon Bishambhar's troops. Then did he realize in his heart of hearts, That his troops were retreating after facing defeat. (19)
lines: The way an insectivorous bird pounces upon white ants,
So did the Singhs pounce upon Bishambhar's troops.
Then did he realize in his heart of hearts,
That his troops were retreating after facing defeat.

blocks.text: Dohra:
Thereupon, dismounting from his horse, Did Bishambhar stand firm in the battlefield. Making a rush at him standing alone, Did the Singhs chop off his head from his body. (20)
lines: Thereupon, dismounting from his horse,
Did Bishambhar stand firm in the battlefield.
Making a rush at him standing alone,
Did the Singhs chop off his head from his body.

blocks.text: Soon after the Singhs had slaughtered Bishambhar, They went on a looting spree among his troops. Many a horse and tents did the Singhs seize, Along with the camels loaded with merchandise. (21)
lines: Soon after the Singhs had slaughtered Bishambhar,
They went on a looting spree among his troops.
Many a horse and tents did the Singhs seize,
Along with the camels loaded with merchandise.

blocks.text: Chaupai:

About twenty thousand camels and horses did they seize, Fully equipped base camp also did they occupy. The market which had plenty of provisions inside, Same did the Singhs and robbers take possession of. (22)
lines: About twenty thousand camels and horses did they seize,
Fully equipped base camp also did they occupy.
The market which had plenty of provisions inside,
Same did the Singhs and robbers take possession of.

blocks.text: The rare treasure that belonged to Bishambhar Dass, Everyone picked up whatever one laid one's hands upon. The Singhs who had been without any weapons of their own, Many a weapon did they pick up to get themselves armed. (23)
lines: The rare treasure that belonged to Bishambhar Dass,
Everyone picked up whatever one laid one's hands upon.
The Singhs who had been without any weapons of their own,
Many a weapon did they pick up to get themselves armed.

blocks.text: Some of the Singhs caught hold of two horses at a time, Better of the two did they mount leaving the inferior one aside. Many a weapon did some of the Singhs pick up, Thus did they get rid of their endemic destitution. (24)
lines: Some of the Singhs caught hold of two horses at a time,
Better of the two did they mount leaving the inferior one aside.
Many a weapon did some of the Singhs pick up,
Thus did they get rid of their endemic destitution.

blocks.text: The heavy artillery cannons they did not carry, Setting these on fire there and then in the field. It was in the year eighteen hundred and eighteen6 , That the Singhs killed Bishambhar and looted his treasure. (25)
lines: The heavy artillery cannons they did not carry,
Setting these on fire there and then in the field.
It was in the year eighteen hundred and eighteen6 ,
That the Singhs killed Bishambhar and looted his treasure.
